workingTitle: JWST measures the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf
coreFacts: Five JWST/NIRCam epochs spanning 2.03 years measured a parallax of 15.7 +1.4/-1.3 milliarcseconds at signal-to-noise 11.5.
The parallax gives a geometric distance of 64 +6/-5 parsecs, about three times farther than previously known Y dwarfs with reliable parallax distances.
The object is classified later than Y1 and has a bolometric luminosity log(Lbol/Lsun) = -7.08 +/- 0.09.
Evolutionary models infer about 8 Jupiter masses and an effective temperature near 300 kelvin, but those physical properties depend on models and an age prior.
Current atmosphere models do not reproduce the full spectral energy distribution; disequilibrium chemistry and vertical mixing are favored, while evidence for water deficiency remains unclear.
sourceStatus: Full primary preprint and abstract read; no secondary source needed for material claims.
caveats: The paper is an unreviewed preprint.
Mass, temperature, radius, and atmospheric interpretation are model-dependent.
Precise spectral typing later than Y1 remains premature.
